title: SLO Dashboards: Structure, Naming, and Required Panels
author: Sergio Costa
body:
## Purpose
This page defines Redwood’s standard structure and naming conventions for **SLO** and **error budget** dashboards across Hosted API and Dedicated tiers. The goal is to make it easy for anyone (oncall, SRE, product, platform engineers) to find the right dashboard quickly, interpret the results consistently, and jump to the right runbooks/policy.

This is a *convention and quality bar* document. It does not redefine SLO targets or SLI math. Refer to:
- **Tiered SLO definitions:** /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/tiered-slo-definitions-hosted-vs-dedicated
- **SLI calculation spec:** /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/sli-spec-success-timeouts-streaming-disconnects
- **Error budget policy & enforcement:** /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/error-budget-policy-and-enforcement

## Scope
Applies to dashboards used for:
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): chat/completions (streaming + non-streaming), embeddings, rerank (when applicable)
- Dedicated: per-customer/pool SLO dashboards and pool readiness/capacity indicators
- Cross-cutting services that materially affect SLOs (e.g., API Gateway, Smart Routing, Control Plane, Runtime) when they have tier-aware SLIs

Out of scope:
- Customer-facing dashboards (Console views follow these same definitions, but may have different UX)
- Private deployments (may reuse templates, but enforcement/standardization is optional initially)

## Principles
1) **Discoverable:** A predictable folder path + naming scheme.
2) **Comparable:** Same panel order and terminology everywhere; same filters.
3) **Actionable:** Every dashboard links to (a) the error budget policy, and (b) the relevant runbook(s).
4) **Tier-aware:** Hosted and Dedicated dashboards must clearly display tier context and avoid mixing signals.
5) **Cardinality-safe:** Dashboards must not require uncontrolled label explosion (see metric cardinality guidance in observability standards).

---

## Dashboard folder structure
Dashboards are organized in the Observability system (Grafana) under a single top-level folder.

### Top-level
**Redwood / Reliability / SLOs**

### Second level (tier)
- **Hosted**
- **Dedicated**
- **Shared Components** (only for tier-aware shared services; avoid using this for generic service dashboards)

### Third level (category)
Hosted:
- **API Endpoints** (customer journeys)
- **Service Contributors** (gateway/routing/runtime contributors to Hosted SLOs)

Dedicated:
- **Customer Pools** (per-customer/pool views)
- **Pool Readiness & Capacity** (scheduler health, provision-to-ready, capacity safety)
- **Service Contributors** (tier-aware signals impacting Dedicated)

Shared Components:
- **Policy & Budgeting** (budget computation jobs, policy engine, gating services)

### Fourth level (region)
Dashboards are grouped by region folder when a dashboard is primarily region-scoped:
- us-east-1
- us-west-2
- eu-west-1
- (…additional active regions)

If a dashboard is intentionally **global** (e.g., global hosted API overview), it lives directly under the category folder and includes a Region filter.

---

## Dashboard naming conventions
All SLO dashboards MUST start with the tag **[SLO]** to distinguish them from service health dashboards.

### Canonical naming template
**[SLO] <Tier> / <Journey or Component> / <Scope>**

Where:
- **Tier**: Hosted | Dedicated
- **Journey or Component**:
  - Journey examples: “Chat Completions (Streaming)”, “Chat Completions (Non-streaming)”, “Embeddings”, “Model Catalog Ops”
  - Component examples: “API Gateway”, “Smart Routing”, “Runtime”, “Control Plane”
- **Scope**: a short descriptor indicating whether this is Global, Region, Pool, or Customer-scoped

### Examples
Hosted API journey dashboards:
- **[SLO] Hosted / Chat Completions (Streaming) / Global**
- **[SLO] Hosted / Chat Completions (Streaming) / us-east-1**
- **[SLO] Hosted / Embeddings / eu-west-1**

Dedicated dashboards:
- **[SLO] Dedicated / Customer Pool / <customer_slug> / us-east-1**
- **[SLO] Dedicated / Pool Readiness / us-west-2**

Shared tier-aware component dashboards:
- **[SLO] Shared / API Gateway / Global (Tier-aware)**
- **[SLO] Shared / Smart Routing / us-east-1 (Tier-aware)**

### Title hygiene requirements
- Do not use internal codenames in titles.
- Include “(Streaming)” explicitly for streaming dashboards.
- If a dashboard is Tier-aware but not Tier-specific, include “(Tier-aware)” in the title.

---

## Required variables (standardized filters)
All SLO dashboards MUST include the following filters (even if defaulted or hidden based on tier).

### Required filters (all tiers)
- **tier**: hosted | dedicated
  - Hosted dashboards should have tier pinned to hosted (still included as a variable for consistency with links).
  - Dedicated dashboards should have tier pinned to dedicated.
- **region**: region name (us-east-1, …)
- **route**: canonical route group (see Route Grouping below)
- **model**: canonical model identifier (e.g., llama-3.1-70b-instruct)
- **window**: time window selector for SLO rollups (e.g., 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 28d)

### Dedicated-only filters
- **customer** (or customer_slug): required for customer pool dashboards
- **pool_id**: required if a customer has multiple pools

Dedicated dashboards containing customer identifiers MUST be placed in a restricted folder and have access controlled (see “Permissions” below).

### Standard variable names
To enable consistent cross-linking and alert → dashboard deep links, use these exact variable names:
- $tier
- $region
- $route
- $model
- $window
- $customer (Dedicated only)
- $pool_id (Dedicated only)

---

## Route grouping standard (for $route)
To avoid dashboard sprawl and metric cardinality blowups, SLO dashboards use **route groups** rather than raw paths.

### Hosted route groups (examples)
- chat.completions.streaming
- chat.completions
- text.completions
- embeddings
- rerank
- models.list
- models.get

Notes:
- Route groups should match the canonical route group taxonomy defined in the SLI spec page.
- If a raw route is needed for an investigation, it belongs in a service-debug dashboard, not an SLO dashboard.

---

## Required dashboard sections and panels
All SLO dashboards must follow this top-to-bottom structure so oncall can “pattern match” quickly.

### Section 1: SLO + error budget at a glance (required)
Panels:
1) **SLO compliance (rolling window)**
   - Show: SLI value vs target for the selected $window (typically 28d default)
   - Include a single-stat “pass/fail” indicator
2) **Error budget remaining**
   - Show remaining budget in % and absolute (e.g., minutes/requests depending on SLI type)
3) **Burn rate (multi-window)**
   - At minimum: 1h/6h and 6h/24h burn rates (or per org standard)
   - Include threshold lines matching the burn-rate alert standard

### Section 2: SLIs (required)
Panels (as applicable by journey):
- **Availability / success rate** (success vs total)
- **Error rate**
  - Separate 5xx from 4xx where policy defines exclusions (e.g., invalid auth not counted)
  - If using “bad event” semantics, label clearly
- **Timeout rate**
- **Latency**
  - Non-streaming: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end
  - Streaming: **TTFT (time to first token)** p50/p95/p99 AND **stream duration** p50/p95/p99 (do not combine)
- **Streaming disconnect rate** (streaming journeys only)
  - Must distinguish: client abort vs server disconnect where available

Each SLI panel must include a short panel description indicating:
- numerator and denominator definition (high-level)
- what is excluded (e.g., invalid auth)
- link to the SLI spec for exact details

### Section 3: Breakdown + top offenders (required)
Panels:
- **By region** (if dashboard is global)
- **By model** (top N models by traffic)
- **By route group** (top N routes)
- **Top offenders table**
  - A single table showing the worst contributors by dimension (region/model/route), with traffic context

Guidance:
- Keep “top N” modest (10–20) to avoid expensive queries.
- Prefer pre-aggregated metrics over ad-hoc log queries.

### Section 4: Correlation context (required)
Panels:
- **Request volume (RPS) and token throughput** (where available)
- **Queueing / saturation** (runtime queue depth, gateway concurrency, routing retries)
- **Fallback / degradation events**
  - e.g., model fallback rate, region failover rate, protective throttling activations

### Section 5: Change and incident overlays (required)
Panels:
- **Deploy markers / release annotations**
  - Deployments for gateway/routing/runtime/control plane affecting the selected tier/region
- **Feature flag / policy changes** (when available)
- **Incidents**
  - Link to incident channel/postmortem when present

---

## Dedicated tier: additional required panels
Dedicated has customer/pool-specific readiness concerns that must be visible alongside request SLIs.

### Dedicated customer pool dashboards MUST include:
- **Pool readiness SLI** (as defined in Dedicated SLO notes)
- **Provision-to-ready time** (p50/p95/p99) for scale-up events (if applicable)
- **Capacity headroom** (allocated vs available GPU, or scheduler capacity signal)
- **Autoscaling actions** (scale events, failed scale events)

### Dedicated Pool Readiness & Capacity dashboards MUST include:
- **Scheduler health** (error rate, latency)
- **Capacity signal integrity** (stale signals, missing heartbeats)
- **Ready vs desired replicas** (or equivalent)
- **Impact estimate** panel (how many customer pools are affected)

---

## Cross-linking requirements (runbooks + policy)
Every SLO dashboard MUST have a “Links” panel at the top (or a persistent dashboard description) containing:
- **Error budget policy & enforcement** (canonical page)
- **Error budget exhaustion response runbook**
- **Service/journey runbook** (gateway/routing/runtime, or journey-specific)
- **Tiered SLO definitions** page

Recommended link formatting:
- “Policy: Error budget enforcement”
- “Runbook: Budget exhaustion response”
- “Runbook: Streaming disconnect spikes” (if applicable)

---

## Permissions and confidentiality
- Hosted dashboards are generally **internal** and broadly visible within Engineering.
- Dedicated customer/pool dashboards are **customer-sensitive** by nature (they may reveal customer identity, workload patterns, or capacity).

Requirements for Dedicated customer dashboards:
1) Place dashboards under **Redwood / Reliability / SLOs / Dedicated / Customer Pools**
2) Apply folder permissions consistent with internal guidance (SRE + Dedicated oncall + limited platform staff)
3) Do not include raw customer identifiers in panel titles; use $customer variable
4) Do not include raw prompt/user content (never query raw payload logs from these dashboards)

If you believe a dashboard should be restricted but it currently is not, file an internal request (see INT-1201) and notify #eng-sre.

---

## Quality checklist (for new or modified SLO dashboards)
Before marking a dashboard “ready”, confirm:
1) Title follows the **[SLO]** naming scheme
2) Folder path matches this standard
3) Required variables exist with standard variable names
4) Required sections exist in the expected order
5) Burn-rate panels match the org standard windows and thresholds
6) Links panel includes policy + runbooks
7) Queries are safe (no unbounded cardinality; no raw route explosion)
8) Dedicated dashboards are permissioned correctly

---

## Ownership and change process
- Primary owner: **Eng Platform / Dashboards & Alerts** (Sergio Costa)
- Standards owner: **Observability Standards** (Allison Grant)
- SLO definitions owner: **SRE** (Aisha Bello)

Changes to this standard:
- Minor edits (typos, clearer wording): direct edit + notify #eng-sre.
- Convention changes affecting many dashboards (variables, naming templates, required panels): open a short review in #eng-platform and #eng-sre, and update this page alongside a bulk change PR or migration plan.

---

## Appendix: Recommended defaults
- Default time range: last **24h** for SLI graphs; last **28d** for SLO/budget rollups
- Default filters:
  - Hosted global dashboards: $region = all, $model = all, $route = all
  - Dedicated customer dashboards: $customer pre-selected, $pool_id pre-selected if possible
- Suggested panel ordering within “SLIs” section:
  1) availability/success
  2) error rate (5xx)
  3) timeouts
  4) latency p95/p99 (or TTFT + stream duration)
  5) disconnect rate (streaming only)

Questions or gaps: post in #eng-sre with a dashboard link and your proposed change.
